messages:
elaine: Quick architecture question — for per-request quality controls, do we expose a numeric hint (0-100) or an explicit bit-preference string (e.g. "fp8", "int8", "4bit")? thinking about future mapping and customer ergonomics.
omar: I vote hint. runtime can map ranges to profiles and we can evolve mapping without breaking callers. header like `x-rw-quality: 85`.
kevin: ops note: default must be safest (max quality) if header missing. also need canary gating for any 4-bit paths.
elaine: agree on default. also worried about long-context cost — maybe only apply lowered precision for tokens beyond some threshold?
omar: prefer we avoid per-token switching inside the model. simpler: routing layer decides profile up front. we can support a param `longtail_threshold=1024` or `longtail_policy=reduce|truncate`.
elaine: sounds pragmatic. can we also surface an explicit `x-rw-max-bit` for customers that want deterministic binding? optional fallback to mapping table.
omar: yep — runtime resolution order: explicit header > quality hint map > tenant default. add telemetry tag `quant_path` with chosen profile. minimal impl: routing decides, inject profile metadata into request envelope before worker.
kevin: ops checklist: add canary flag, telemetry, alert if >1% of requests hit experimental 4-bit, and rollback runbook. also add cost chargeback tag. :thumbsup:
elaine: example header snippet for docs: ```
X-RW-Quality: 70
X-RW-Max-Bit: fp8   # optional
X-RW-Longtail-Policy: reduce
```
omar: implementation todo: (1) add header parsing in gateway, (2) mapping table + simple DSL, (3) runtime tag plumbing, (4) canary config in deploy. I'll open a short RFC/PR for the mapping table semantics.
kevin: canary windows + dashboard needed too. ops-bot: deploy scheduled for canary toggle at 18:00 UTC.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary toggle at 1715007600 by kevin
elaine: cool — thanks. i'll draft the docs page and include examples and recommended defaults for customer-facing SDKs.
omar: great. leaving this thread to the RFC/PR for details.
